source_conversation.content: I'm on my laptop in Chrome and one website keeps opening pop-up windows over everything. How do I stop that one site from doing it?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states the device and app (laptop, Chrome) and asks to stop one named-by-role site from opening pop-ups, which the site-specific block steps cover.
candidates.target:
Here's how to block pop-ups from one website in Chrome on your computer:
1. Open Chrome and click **More**, then **Settings**.
2. Click **Privacy and security**, then **Site Settings**, then **Pop-ups and redirects**.
3. Under 'Allowed to send pop-ups and use redirects,' find the site.
4. Click **More** next to the site, then **Block**.
5. If the site isn't listed, click **Add** next to 'Not allowed to send pop-ups or use redirects,' enter the site's web address, and then click **Add**. To cover a whole domain, use the pattern [*.]example.com.
candidates.author_note: Covers the Settings path, finding the site under Allowed, More then Block, and the Add branch when the site is not listed. Source gap: the default-setting choices are not named on the page and are not covered.

source_conversation.content: The payment window for my bank won't open in Chrome on my computer. There's a small note in the address bar about pop-ups. How do I let it open?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states the device and app and describes the blocked pop-up in the address bar, which matches the allow-a-site steps.
candidates.target:
Chrome can let this pop-up open:
1. In the address bar, click **Pop-up blocked**.
2. Click the link for the pop-up you want to check.
3. To always allow pop-ups for this site, select **Always allow pop-ups and redirects from [site]**, and then click **Done**.
candidates.author_note: Covers clicking Pop-up blocked, opening the pop-up link, and the optional always-allow choice for the site with Done. Only the steps the user still needs are given.

source_conversation.content: I'm on Windows 11 and links keep opening in Edge when I click them. I want Chrome to be the one that opens links. How do I set that?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states Windows 11 and wants Chrome set for links, which the Windows 11 steps cover; the Windows 10 passage is an inapplicable distractor.
candidates.target:
Here's how to make Chrome your default browser on Windows 11. If you don't have Google Chrome on your computer yet, first download and install Chrome.
1. Select **Start**.
2. Select **Settings**, then **Apps**, then **Default apps**.
3. Under 'Set defaults for applications,' in the search box, enter **Chrome**.
4. Select **Google Chrome**.
5. At the top, next to 'Make Google Chrome your default browser,' select **Set default**.
6. To make sure the change is applied to the correct file types, review the list under 'Set default file types or link types.'
candidates.author_note: Covers the install-first note, the Settings, Apps, Default apps path, the search and selection, Set default, and the file-type check. No other Windows version is covered.

source_conversation.content: I want links to open in Chrome on my Windows 10 computer. Can you walk me through making it the default?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states Windows 10 and asks to make Chrome the default, which the Windows 10 steps cover; the Windows 11 passage is an inapplicable distractor.
candidates.target:
Here's how to make Chrome your default browser on Windows 10. If you don't have Google Chrome on your computer yet, first download and install Chrome.
1. Select **Start**, and then select **Settings**.
2. To open your default apps, select **System**, and then **Default apps** if you have the original version.
3. Select **Apps**, and then **Default apps** if you have the Creators Update.
4. At the bottom, under 'Web browser,' select your current browser.
5. In the 'Choose an app' window, select **Google Chrome**.
candidates.author_note: Covers both Windows 10 versions as branches (Original version and Creators Update), the install-first note, and the Web browser choice. No Windows 11 steps are included.

source_conversation.content: There's a device listed under my Google account that I don't recognize. What should I do about it?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states an unrecognized device on their Google Account, and the page advises signing out of devices that do not belong to the user, with steps to do so.
candidates.target:
Sign out of the device if it doesn't belong to you. In your Google Account:
1. Go to your Google Account (myaccount.google.com).
2. Tap **Security & sign-in**.
3. Under 'Your devices,' tap **Manage all devices**.
4. Tap the device you want to remove, and then tap **Sign out**.
candidates.author_note: Protective action first: sign out of a device that does not belong to the user, with the four Google Account steps. Source gap: the Secure your account steps for unfamiliar activity were not fetched and are not covered.

source_conversation.content: I sold my old phone last month, but two entries with the same name still show under my devices in my Google account. How do I remove them?

candidates.decision_basis: The user states the old device is no longer theirs and shows two entries with the same name, which the sign-out steps and the same-device-name condition cover.
candidates.target:
Sign out of the old device first, so that no other device keeps account access.
1. Go to your Google Account (myaccount.google.com).
2. Tap **Security & sign-in**.
3. Under 'Your devices,' tap **Manage all devices**.
4. Tap the device you want to remove, and then tap **Sign out**.
5. If several sessions show the same device name, sign out of all the sessions with this device name.
candidates.author_note: Protective action first, then the four sign-out steps and the same-device-name condition with its own step. Source gap: the page names no option to sign out of all devices at once, so none is offered.
